consensus_findings.description: Critical: The shared advisory lock serializes a different-sequence submit/reconcile race but does not make its outcome order-independent. If reconciliation for sequence N commits first, a delayed keyed submit for stale sequence N-1 can acquire the lock afterward and insert a new active row, violating the requirement that the reconciled current sequence be the only active projection row.

Nit: The new reconcile endpoint requires policy denial behavior, but the plan never identifies the authorization action. The current native and Cedar inventories know `submit_work`, not `reconcile_work`, while the coordinator package cannot modify the policy schema or policy files under its declared write scope.

Nit: The verification gates promise direct MCP parity but run no dedicated direct-MCP test module and no whole coordinator test directory. A new direct MCP test file can therefore be omitted from both package and integration gates while all declared commands remain green.
The plan correctly places same-key idempotency in PostgreSQL with a partial unique expression index and keeps unkeyed submissions backward compatible.
The persist-before-project seam and resume re-derivation keep filesystem state authoritative and give the non-transactional crash window an explicit repair path.
